column1: # coverage-accepted-removals.tsv -- justified outright deletions with NO re-home target,
# for the coverage-parity gate (consumed via 'coverage-parity.sh diff --accept').
# Distinct from a re-home: this records keyed assertions DELETED outright because what
# they asserted is already covered elsewhere by construction (e.g. a redundant nested
# peer-suite exit-code check whose peer already runs standalone via the run-all.sh
# glob, so there is no new key to name as a re-home target).
# A net-removed/reduced key is EXCUSED as an accepted removal iff it is listed below
# with a NON-EMPTY justification. This does not weaken the gate: the diff still flags
# every removal; the only pass route is an explicit, justified, human-reviewed entry
# Schema (TAB-separated, 4 fields); '#'-comment and blank lines are ignored:
# This forward-going list starts EMPTY. The 7 work-024 delivery-002 rows were relative
# to the pre-work-024 merge-base and are already absorbed into master, so they are NOT
# seeded here. Append one reviewed row per future accepted removal.

column4: The 20 internal READMEs were deleted (FR-7), so canonical/skills/aid-monitor/README.md no longer exists and an existence assert on it cannot pass. Nothing is lost: the file was internal, installed into no tree, and resolved by no instruction.

Asserted the BUG -> /aid-fix routing in the deleted README. The same routing is still asserted against SHIPPING files by DMR03a (aid-monitor/SKILL.md) and DMR01a/DMR02a (references/state-route.md), so this was a duplicate of live coverage, not coverage itself.

Asserted the Change Request -> /aid-triage routing in the deleted README. Still asserted against shipping files by DMR03b (SKILL.md) and DMR01b/DMR02b (state-route.md), so the deletion de-duplicated rather than reduced.

One of the 7 CANONICAL_BODIES sample paths was aid/templates/delivery-blueprint-template.md, deleted when BLUEPRINT.md was retired (the delivery definition now lives in the delivery own PLAN.md stanza). The KEY survives -- the label is path-normalised to <PATH> and the 6 remaining sample paths still emit it -- so only the emission count drops. The property asserted (a canonical body with no tool-root references renders byte-identically across install trees) is unchanged and still sampled 6 ways. Listed here in case the gate counts the reduction; inert if it does not.
